issues.acceptance: A representative native-renderer before/after capture reports raw frame times, one-percent low, hitch count, CPU/GPU attribution, and named script hot paths with 3, 5, 10, and 18 active enemies. Enemy separation is computed once from a cached stable roster per physics cycle, QA instrumentation performs no per-frame deep state snapshot or scene-wide scan in ordinary play, and AI behavior/spacing remains unchanged. llvmpipe evidence is recorded only as collector evidence.
issues.actual: scripts/enemy_agent.gd rebuilds and sorts the complete fusepoint_enemy group inside _separation_safe_velocity(), then invokes that admission path multiple times per navigation cycle for every active enemy. At the same time, the main scene runs RuntimeQualificationProbe in PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, deep-calls mission/roster/weapon state and periodically scans the complete scene tree for audio players. With 18 active enemies these are credible CPU hitch hot paths and must be profiled on a native renderer; the llvmpipe collector result cannot attribute the user's stutter to their computer.
issues.expected: Ordinary gameplay performs bounded enemy steering and lightweight production work per frame; deep QA snapshots run only on demand or at a bounded debug sampling cadence.
issues.next_action: Capture native-renderer CPU/GPU profiler evidence, remove duplicate peer scans and sorts, and gate or sample QA-only deep observation.
issues.observed: scripts/enemy_agent.gd rebuilds and sorts the complete fusepoint_enemy group inside _separation_safe_velocity(), then invokes that admission path multiple times per navigation cycle for every active enemy. At the same time, the main scene runs RuntimeQualificationProbe in PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, deep-calls mission/roster/weapon state and periodically scans the complete scene tree for audio players. With 18 active enemies these are credible CPU hitch hot paths and must be profiled on a native renderer; the llvmpipe collector result cannot attribute the user's stutter to their computer.
issues.summary: Always-on diagnostics and repeated enemy peer scans risk runtime hitches

diagnosis.root_cause: Loop 69 left the combat_readability surface open because it delivered partial fixtures and honest telemetry around known gaps, but did not remove the candidate-side blockers: rifle enemies still bind pistol-authored clips, the enemy matrix is not proven through full combat transitions, and the story/feedback presenter still lacks complete black-box lifecycle coverage. The next loop must use a materially different closure strategy: replace or restore animation bindings instead of relabeling clips, separate encounter prepare from advance for full AI evidence, and make story cues plus feedback cleanup directly retestable across branch lifecycles.

stop_conditions: Do not modify run-owned evidence, frozen PRD/config, asset-pool source packages, imported raw source assets, or ignored Godot cache/import folders.

strategy.rationale: Active debt is above the convergence floor and the same work items have repeated across loops, so this plan caps scope to three implementation families that partition the four host-selected active issues exactly once: animation binding, enemy combat matrix evidence readiness, and combat feedback/story readability. The plan avoids another transform-tuning or telemetry-only pass by requiring candidate-owned repairs plus deterministic branch-local retest hooks where full ordinary replay is too expensive.
